h: פָּרָשַׁת פָּרָה, מַאֲמָר ב׳ Parshas Parah — Maamar Bais

p: פִּי צַדִּיק יֶהְגֶּה חָכְמָה [תְּהִלִּים לז, ל]
"The mouth of the tzaddik utters wisdom" (Tehillim 37:30).
in line with what they said
we call it Torah she'b'al peh."
And in the holy Zohar (vol. III 201b):
the mouth of Hashem; see there.
And this is what they said
"The day of Shabbos in the year,
and the mouth in the soul."
And we have already said that certainly
that the mouth was created on Shabbos,
עִם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא [בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, ט-יב]
Rather, on Shabbos the power was created
"My words which I have placed in your mouth,"
and it will be the mouth of Hashem.
And the matter is as we have said (Maamar 1):
through the reading of the parsha,
while the enactment to read it
the power of Torah she'b'al peh —
Hashem Yisbarach too reads the parsha
and occupies Himself with its halachos.
And this is what is said: "The mouth of the tzaddik" —
the mouth of the Tzaddik of the world —
because it is named for the voice,
which is the aspect of wisdom
of the moon, Torah she'b'al peh,
regarding the wording of what they said:
Who was sitting and occupied," etc.
That is, the matter of Parshas Parah
is that it purifies from the tumah of a corpse;
that is, it repairs the entire root
of the corruption of the serpent
which comes to repair the "abundance of anger."
And this is what they said in the Pesikta there (siman 13)
and the Midrash (Rabbah and Tanchuma, Chukas, ibid.):
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to Moshe:
"To you I reveal the reason of the Parah,
but for others it is a chok," etc.
are destined to be visible to you
in the World to Come," etc.
of the root of the corruption
"He will swallow up death forever," etc.
But Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who knew nothing at all of evil —
the house was filled with light
he understood that one can repair
as it will be in the future.
And in truth he did not die,
"Just as there he stands and serves,
so too here he stands and serves."
'and no man knows his burial place'
That is, no person at all
how it could be conceived regarding a man
like Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
that the matter of burial be written of him,
since he is alive and enduring,
for he knew nothing of any evil.
But "for others it is a chok" —
that is, for others who corrupted,
the matter of the Parah is a chok,
for it is impossible to understand
how all the blemish will be repaired
and how there can be purity
for the tumah of a corpse.
For this depth will not be revealed
as it is written, "He will swallow up death forever,"
all the corruption of the serpent.
And the Midrash and Pesikta conclude:
it is not written 'I will do'
for Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues.
Things that were not revealed to Moshe
were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues.
וְכׇל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ [אִיּוֹב כח, י]
'And every precious thing his eye saw' (Iyov 28:10) —
this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues."
one can repair the "abundance of anger"
And this is the power of Torah she'b'al peh,
the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
and it is the fiftieth gate
that is revealed to baalei teshuvah.
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who knew nothing at all of evil;
and it was revealed to Rabbi Akiva,
who was a son of converts.
And the root of the Torah she'b'al peh
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
that was included within the Torah she'b'chsav,
when nothing would have been given them
but the five Chumashei Torah, etc.
and all of Torah she'b'al peh would have been
included in the five Chumashei Torah.
And this is in the secret of Daas,
and it is the matter of halachah l'Moshe mi'Sinai,
that it is from Sinai, from Heaven;
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him
This is not so of Rabbi Akiva,
who was a son of converts;
which is unique to baalei teshuvah.
in the manner of what they said
and behold it was very good'" (Bereishis 1:31),
which is expounded regarding everything that is the opposite of good,
that it exists so that it should be very good;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
and in the manner of what they said (Zohar II 184a):
except that which emerges from within darkness,
And this is when willful sins become like merits
for then is revealed the light
which alludes to the deeds of the wicked,
as they said in Bereishis Rabbah (2:5);
"'If your sins be like scarlet' — like these years
from the six days of Creation," etc.
That is, it is then revealed
that such was His will, may He be blessed,
and then "they shall be white as snow,"
That is, the aspect of the First Utterance,
that which shines out of the opposite,
light that emerges from within darkness.
one can repair the root of the corruption,
And this is what they said in the Pesikta (ibid., siman 7):
כׇּל זֶה נִסִּיתִי בַחׇכְמָה וְגוֹמֵר [קֹהֶלֶת ז, כג]
"'All this I tested with wisdom,' etc. (Koheles 7:23) —
into all the parshiyos of the Torah
and into all the depths of wisdom
I entered and grasped them," etc.
he cried out, 'I will become wise,'" etc.
And so it is in the Midrash
"But the parsha of the Parah Adumah —
but it is far from me,'"
where is it alluded to in this pasuk
that it refers to the parsha of the Parah Adumah?
which is the aspect of "the mouth of Hashem,"
understanding one thing from within another.
And Daas, which is the inwardness of Keser,
that shines forth from the dew of Atika,
which is also of the aspect of Daas,
and it is the "abundance of wisdom"
that is effective to repair the "abundance of anger,"
And Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
"like the sand that is on the seashore."
And it says in the Midrash (Chukas, ibid.):
Just as the sand makes for it
so that it not go out and flood the world,
so that he not sin," etc.
That is, the wisdom of Torah she'b'al peh
which he merited from Hashem Yisbarach in a dream,
that this is the Torah she'b'al peh.
the power of Torah she'b'al peh
which is the power of Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues,
And this is the depth and the matter
of the purification of the Parah:
to repair the root of the corruption.
And regarding Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
among the kings one did arise,"
to understand from my own side
the matter of the Parah Adumah,
to repair the root of the blemish
understanding from within the Torah she'b'chsav —
for he merited only, from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him.
And so, after the corruption was recorded
concerning Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
the Men of the Great Assembly wished
those who have no share, chas v'shalom
that is, he lacked this power
of David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה [עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה, א].
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah (Avodah Zarah 5a).
Until a heavenly voice went forth, etc.
for in truth Shlomo did not sin at all
And in truth it will be Mashiach
for all of Yisrael are bound at the root
דִּרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ כּוּ׳ [בְּרָכוֹת יז, א]
"our will is to do Your will," etc. (Berachos 17a),
and then the root of the blemish will be repaired
and death will be swallowed up forever.
for the parsha is from Torah she'b'chsav
and the enactment to read it
And on Shabbos, which is the time
for all agree that on Shabbos
the Torah was given to Yisrael
and it says in the holy Zohar
we call it Torah she'b'al peh"
And it is the time of the root
of Torah she'b'chsav and Torah she'b'al peh.
Therefore it was enacted to read
for their being redeemed in Nisan.
And this is what Rashi wrote
that they make their Pesach offerings in purity."
that they will be redeemed in Nisan;
through the reading of Parshas Parah,
from all the tumah of the yetzer hara,
they will be redeemed in Nisan
and make their Pesach offerings in purity.

paragraphs.text: Sefer Yetzirah 4, letter tav — “He made the letter tav reign, bound a crown to it, and through it formed the moon in the world, the Sabbath day in the year, and the mouth in the person.” This is the recension that assigns the moon to tav. The Gra recension also associates tav with Sabbath and the mouth, but assigns Jupiter rather than the moon. Rav Tzadok’s point here concerns Sabbath and speech.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Yisro 13 — “Like Yaakov Avinu, who was like Adam HaRishon before the corruption and knew nothing of bodily pleasure, and so did not die; so too we find of Moshe Rabbeinu, ‘Moshe did not die.’” Rav Tzadok there gives the reason. Death came through the serpent’s corruption, so one wholly untouched by it is not subject to death. That is why Moshe could grasp the parah’s reason, a purity that reaches the root of death.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 13 — “For this purpose they were given the commandments of Sabbath and the red heifer there at Marah, and were commanded concerning judgments. Sabbath teaches: See, the blessed God gives you a commandment through which you serve Him by ceasing from activity; why, then, complain? The red heifer points toward the future, for in the future the Lord will be One and His name One; then service will cease, and there will be no anger. Judgments teach order: do not constantly think of forcing the hour in order to attain all this goodness. Everything must proceed in an order that becomes fixed in the heart without alteration.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: The Ishbitzer explicitly joins the red heifer with the future abolition of anger, and places it beside Sabbath’s sanctification of cessation. This clarifies the maamar’s link between Parah, the repair of the primordial damage, and Sabbath as a present anticipation of that future.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Akeidas Yitzchak, Sha'ar 79 — on “things not revealed to Moshe were revealed to Rabbi Akiva”: “The prophet knows the future only in general… but the sage knows the particulars too, and understands the cause of each detail.” The Akeidah reads the midrash as the sage’s power of detail. Rav Tzadok takes it further: the Oral Torah draws its power to repair from the very corruption Moshe never knew.

paragraphs.text: Shaar Maamarei Razal, Shabbat, passage beginning “Let us return to Rabbi Akiva” — “Rabbi Akiva attained what Moses our teacher did not attain, for Moses our teacher attained only forty-nine gates, while he attained the fiftieth.... Our Sages said that the Holy One showed Moses each generation and its leaders, and showed him Rabbi Akiva expounding the crowns of the letters.... ‘Be silent; thus he ascended in thought’—that is, be silent, for through such a death he ascended in thought and to the place of the eyes.” The specific statement about the fiftieth gate appears in the comment introduced “Shmuel said,” identifying Rabbi Shmuel Vital’s annotation within the Lurianic collection. Rav Tzadok develops its relation to repentance here; the annotation itself explains Rabbi Akiva’s attainment through his martyrdom. Rav Tzadok states outright in Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer 1, that Rabbi Akiva was the root of Torah she'b'al peh, “as is stated in the writings of the Arizal.”

The same link between converts and the Oral Torah explains why Matan Torah stands in Parshas Yisro.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Seitzei 15 — “Wherever ‘halachah l’Moshe miSinai’ is said, it does not mean the halachos were handed to Moshe… what was given to Moshe was the power to derive them from the Torah through his pilpul.” This spells out what Moshe’s Oral Torah “contained in the Written Torah” means. The halachah is drawn out of the text itself. It is not a separate tradition added beside it.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 21b — “One said: ‘Among prophets there arose none, but among kings there did arise [one like Moses].’ How, then, do I explain, ‘Kohelet sought to find desirable words’? Kohelet sought to adjudicate matters of the heart without witnesses or warning. A heavenly voice went forth and said: ‘Words of truth written uprightly’—‘By the testimony of two witnesses....’” The comparison concerns Solomon’s wisdom. The same passage nonetheless limits judgment to the Torah’s rules of evidence.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 104b — “Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: They sought to count one more. The image of his father came and prostrated itself before them, but they paid it no heed. Fire came from heaven and singed their benches, but they paid it no heed. A heavenly voice went forth: ‘One who placed My house before his own—and moreover built My house in seven years, but his own in thirteen—shall stand before kings, not before the obscure.’ ... A heavenly voice went forth: ‘Is it from you that He should repay, because you reject it? For you must choose, and not I?’” The builder of the Temple is Solomon. The debate concerns adding him to the Mishnah’s list of kings lacking a share in the World to Come; the heavenly intervention rejects that human judgment.

rich.text: Shabbat 56b

— “Rabbi Shemuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: Whoever says that Solomon sinned is mistaken, for it is said, ‘His heart was not whole with the Lord his God like the heart of David his father’: it was not like David his father’s heart, but he did not sin.... Because he ought to have protested against his wives and did not protest, Scripture accounts it to him as though he sinned.”
